Mohammad Abul Kashem Bhuiyan for AB Roy Chowdhury, Advocate—For Opposite Party No. 1.

Vs.
Md Shafiullah Patwari and others ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
2. Predecessor-father of petitioners in Civil Revision Case Lutfor Rahman had been pre-emptor in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1984 and first-defendant in Title Suit No. 10 of 1996. On his death petitioners stood substituted as heirs and heirs petitioners had been respondents in Title Appeal. First-opposite party of Civil Revision Case had been second-pre-emptee-opposite party of pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and plaintiff in suit and appellant in appeal. Second-fourth opposite parties of Civil Revision Case were first third-fourth Pre-emptee opposite parties in pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and second-fourth defendants in suit and respondents in appeal. Petitioners in Civil Revision Case shall be referred to hereinafter as defendants-petitioners. First opposite party of Civil Revision shall be described as plaintiff-opposite party. 

 Plaintiff-opposite party impleading petitioners and Second-Fourth opposite parties and other persons as defendants instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 10 of 1996 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kachua, Chandpur for a declaration that ex parte order dated 24-4-1988 recorded in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1984 is fraudulent, illegal, collusive and plaintiff is not bound by ex parte order. Core averments embodied in plaint are: 

 a. Summons of the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case had not been at all served upon plaintiff-opposite party and the same had been fraudulently suppressed. Second-opposite party Torab Ali is not the agent (Karjkarok) of plaintiff-opposite party and, as such Second opposite party got no legal authority to accept any summons on behalf of plaintiff-opposite party. Predecessor of petitioners obtained a parte order through fraudulent suppression of summons upon plaintiff-opposite party. Plaintiff-opposite party had been abroad during the period of alleged service of summons. Plaintiff-First opposite party was not at all aware of pre-emption proceeding against him and he only on 1-4-1995 became aware of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and, also, ex parte order against him from his cousin brother (ফুফাত ভাই) Monu Patwari Monu Patwari was given Power of Attorney to take proper steps in the matter. Monu Patwari obtained all papers on 20-1-1996 and laid suit in Court seeking relief stated above. 

 b. Plaintiff-opposite party had strained relationship with his father and brothers, Second-Fourth opposite parties, in respect of purchase of land under Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case who in order to deprive him of land purchased only by him did not communicate any information to him in regard to Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case. 

 c. In the event of any sort of knowledge of Pre-emption proceeding against him plaintiff-opposite party would have definitely put up contest in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case. 

 d. Plaintiff-opposite party sustained irreparable loss on account of ex parte order of pre-emption against him. 

 a. Summons of the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case had been duly served upon plaintiff-opposite party as well as Second-Fourth opposite parties and plaintiff-opposite party had been well aware of pre-emption proceeding and with an ulterior motive did not lay any written objection against Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case. 

 b. Plaintiff-opposite party and Second-Fourth opposite parties are full brothers and purchasers of land under Pre-emption proceeding. 

 d. Plaintiff-opposite party had been in the house when service of summons had been effected. 

 e. Plaintiff-opposite party constructed house on raising pre-emption proceeding land by earth long after institution of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case. 

 iii. Is the order dated 20-4-1988 passed in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1984 illegal and binding upon plaintiff? 

 iv. Is the plaintiff entitled to relief sought for? 

 6. Learned Assistant Judge, Kachua, Chandpur as trial Judge decided first issue in favour of plaintiff-opposite party. Learned trial Judge held that suit as framed is maintainable. 

 7. Leaned Trial Judge decided Issue No. II against plaintiff-opposite party and held that suit is barred by limitation. In deciding said issue learned Trial Judge found that plaintiff had been aware of case long before accrual of cause of action to lay suit and plaintiff failed to prove that he on 1-4-1995 became aware of the disputed case. 

 8. Learned Trial Judge decided Third Issue against plaintiff-opposite party. In deciding issue learned Trial Judge rendered decision that summons upon plaintiff had been served in accordance with law and there was no ground to accept the contention pressed into service from plaintiff that summons of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case was not served upon plaintiff and plaintiff had been aware of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case. With the above decisions learned Trial Judge dismissed suit. Judgment had been handed down on 30-10-1997. 

 9. Plaintiff-opposite party could not reconcile to verdict awarded upon him by learned Trial Judge and having felt dissatisfied carried an appeal being Title Appeal No. 183 of 1997 before learned District Judge, Chandpur. Learned Subordinate Judge (Joint District Judge), First Court, Chandpur heard appeal, allowed it, set aside Judgment and Decree passed in Title Suit No. 10 of 1996 and decreed suit in favour of plaintiff-opposite party. In awarding decree in favour of plaintiff-opposite party on allowing appeal and turning down judgment and decree recorded in Title Suit No. 10 of 1996 learned Appellate Judge rendered following decisions: 

 i. It has been proved beyond any doubt that summons upon plaintiff Md Shafiullah Patwari in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No 66 of 1984 had not been served directly. In rendering said decision learned Appellate Judge took into account Exhibit-Ka i.e. return of service of summons upon plaintiff-opposite party and, also, evidence of DW 3, Process Server. 

 ii. Plaintiff-opposite party at the relevant time had been out of country. In arriving at the said finding learned Appellate Judge took into account passport and visa submitted by plaintiff-opposite party. Pre-emptor concealed present address of pre-emptee second opposite party (plaintiff-opposite party) and that can be characterized as fraud in the language of law and by the fraud practiced proceeding of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case has been vitiated or has been rendered inoperative. 

 iii. In proof of due service of summons upon Pre-emptee Second-opposite party (plaintiff) defendant of Title Suit only examined process server Belayet, DW 3 but did not examine Mokabila witnesses Abdul Mazid and Aminuddin. Without examination of Mokabila witnesses in regard to service of summons it could not be said that summons had been duly served. In rendering decision reliance had been put upon a Judicial decision in Upendra Chandra Rishi and others vs Sufia Begum 42 DLR (AD) 285. 

 iv. Summons having not been duly served and plaintiff having been abroad the finding reached by Lower Court in respect of establishment of knowledge on the part of plaintiff and finding that suit stood barred by limitation was not justified and Lower Court did not properly analyse fact and law and justice had been infringed by decision rendered by Lower Court. 

 11. Mr Shah Monzurul Hoque, learned Counsel appeared for defendants-petitioners. Plaintiff-opposite party is represented by Mr Mohammad Abul Kashem Bhuiyan, learned Counsel. 

 12. Thrust of contention pressed into service from side of defendants-petitioners is that in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case summons upon Second-opposite party of the case had been duly served and service of summons had been proved by process server DW 3 and plaintiff-opposite party had been at home and had been well aware of pre-emption proceeding but did not put up contest in case and got pre-emption case allowed ex parte against him. 

 13. Other branch of contention advanced is that three brothers of plaintiff-opposite party contested Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and it was allowed on contest against them and miscellaneous appeal carried by them, also, stood dismissed and plaintiff-opposite party had been set up by his brothers with ulterior motive. 

 14. Third and last branch of contention put forth is that plaintiff-opposite party could not substantiate alleged date of knowledge of the order allowing Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and suit was barred by limitation. 

 15. Contentions so raised has been hit back from side of plaintiff-opposite party pressing into service counter-contentions that summons upon plaintiff-opposite party had been fraudulently suppressed and he was quite in darkness of pre-emption proceeding against him as well as of the ex parte order in case and fraud having been practiced in obtaining ex parte order through fraudulent suppression of summons, ex parte order is liable to be adjudged as illegal, collusive and void and the same cannot be binding upon plaintiff-opposite party. 

 16. Next branch of contention surged forward is that plaintiff-opposite party could well prove his first knowledge through legal evidence and suit was filed within statutory period of limitation as fixed by law. Article 95 of The Limitation Act has been relied upon in support of contention. 

 i. Whether non-service of summons upon plaintiff-opposite party is a valid ground for knocking down the order dated 24-4-1988 recorded in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case 

 21. Plaintiff-opposite party asserted that service of summons upon him in Pre-emption case had been fraudulently suppressed and service upon defendants-Second opposite party on his behalf is not at all a valid and lawful service and for non-service of summons he was kept quite in darkness of the whole pre-emption proceeding which terminated in an ex parte order against him on 24-4-1988. Defendants-petitioners took firm stand that summons upon plaintiff-opposite party in the case had been duly served and he had been at home and, as such, he was well aware of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case against him and, also, ex parte order recorded in the case. 

 22. Pivotal war of words, thus, is whether service of summons upon plaintiff-opposite party in Preemption Miscellaneous Case was a valid service or not. 

 28. Exhibit A, Service Return indicates that summons of plaintiff-opposite party in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case had been served upon his brother Torab Ali, Second-opposite party and Second-opposite party accepted summons for and on behalf of plaintiff-opposite party. In the Return it is not at all stated that process server conducted a search and substantial effort and had undertaken proper inquiries to locate plaintiff-opposite party and to effect personal service of summons upon him. Process server DW 3 standing on witness box laid bare evidence that he served summons of First-Fourth opposite parties upon First-opposite party (Torab Ali) and he submitted report accordingly. Evidence of DW 3 is extracted hereunder: 

 It was duty of process server DW 3, to take pain to find out Second-opposite party of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case to effect service upon him and he should have guaranteed proper inquiry in respect of whereabouts of Second-opposite party. In the absence of any attempt on part of process server DW 3 for causing personal service upon Second-opposite party (plaintiff opposite party) of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case service upon plaintiff-opposite party cannot be held to be valid service of summons. 

 36. Second-opposite party, though, a full brother of plaintiff-opposite party got no legal authority to accept summons for the latter. Second-opposite party is not the agent of plaintiff-opposite party. It is well settled that an agent must be an authorized person and Agentnama must be in writing. In order to treat a service on agent valid it was to be established that agent was duly authorised to accept service on behalf of plaintiff-opposite party. In Muhammad Idrees Barry and Co Lahore vs Commissioner of Income Tax, Punjab and NWFP Lahore PLD 1957 (WP) 270 it has been laid down that an authority to accept service of process must be in writing. In Messers Idrees Barry and Co vs Commissioner of Income Tax, West Pakistan PLD 1960 (WP) Lahore 852 it has been stated that authority to accept service of notice as agent must be in writing. In Hazari Dasi vs Daiba Charm: Mandal 26 DLR 3 it has been held: 

 37. In service return there had not been any declaration/verification by process server in respect of due service of summons upon Second-opposite party in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case (plaintiff-opposite party). Service returns bears only the writing of Nazir in the terms that writing are true and service has been duly effected. In the absence of declaration made and subscribed by process server, service return cannot be accepted as evidence of due service. Service return further manifests that there were two Mokabila witnesses, namely, Abdul Mazid and Aminuddin, and names of Mokabila witnesses had been written by process server himself and signature of Mokabila witnesses do not at all appear in service return. Process server was required to obtain signatures of Mokabila witnesses and in the absence of such signature, process server was required to explain in his report why service of Mokabila witnesses could not be obtained No such explanation had been offered by process server in service return. Two Mokabila witnesses had not been examined from side of pre-emptors (defendants-petitioners) in proof of service of summons upon Second-opposite party Torab Ali for and on behalf of plaintiff-opposite party. In the face of serious challenge hurled from side of plaintiff-opposite party in regard to service of summons, it was the duty and responsibility on the part of defendants-petitioners to place Mokabila witnesses on witness box in support of service of summons. Defendant-petitioners, thus, failed to discharge onus of proof that service of summons upon plaintiff-opposite party had been duly and lawfully effected. In Upendra Chandra Rishi and others vs Sufia Begum and others 42 DLR (AD) 285 summons had been served upon defendant by process server without noting names and addresses of Mokabila witnesses. Process server appeared in court as witness in proof of his return but Mokabila witness in whose presence summons was alleged to have been served had not been examined. It had been held that mere personal appearance of process server as a witness in Court did not render the report of process server in respect of service of summons upon defendant acceptable. 

 38. This takes me to another aspect of the matter. It is asserted from side of defendants-petitioners that plaintiff-opposite party's had been in his house. In the event of plaintiff-opposite party's staying in house, service of summons was required to be caused upon him personally and service was not to be effected upon Second-opposite party Torab Ali. From the case set up by defendants-petitioners as to plaintiff-opposite party's staying in his house during the period of service of summons it had been established that service of summons upon plaintiff-opposite party was absolutely invalid. 

 39. Positive case put forward from side of plaintiff-opposite party that he was abroad and not in Bangladesh and that case came up from the lips of plaintiff-opposite party when he stood on witness box. Defendants-petitioners, on the other hand, took stand that plaintiff-opposite party had been in his house during the course of service of summons upon latter. Plaintiff-opposite party appeared to have discharged his initial onus and onus shifted upon defendant-petitioners and defendants-petitioners through legal evidence could not prove that during the period of service of summons plaintiff-opposite party was in the country and he was not abroad. 

 40. Taking into account pleadings of parties, evidences, especially evidence of DW 3 and materials brought on record, especially Exhibit 1, service return, and fact and circumstances of the case, I am of this considered view that Summons upon plaintiff-opposite party had not been served in accordance with law and service was invalid and same had been fraudulently suppressed. 

 41. Plaintiff-opposite party put forward a case that he was not aware of Pre-emption proceeding as well as ex parte order of Pre-emption against him and he became aware of ex parte order on 1-4-1995. PW 3, though, did not specifically mention the date when Monu Mia informed of pre-emption of land by Lutfe Alam (Lutfor Rahman predecessor of defendants-petitioners) but stated that about two years back. Evidence of PW 3 was recorded on 20-9-1997 and date 1-4-1995 would be about two years back of date 20-9-1997. PW 3 is a rustic/village man. He was not supposed to state the exact date. It is well-nigh to remember that human memory is fleeting and mathematical precision is not at all expected from a rustic/village witness like PW 3. Learned Appellate Judge found exception with the finding of learned Trial Judge on the point of limitation and held that Trial Judge was not at all justified in holding the suit to be barred by limitation. No exception can be taken to the decision arrived at by learned Appellate Judge. Date of knowledge had been stated to be on 1-4-1995 and suit was filed on 23-1-1996 which is within the period of limitation fixed by law. Articles 95 and 120 of The Limitation Act can be conveniently pressed into service in this regard. My dispassionate view is that the Suit cannot be said to have been barred by limitation. Learned Trial Judge was not justified in holding the suit to be barred by limitation. 

 42. Plaintiff-opposite party brought forth case that fraud had been practiced in causing service of summons upon him and by means of fraud he had been kept out from the knowledge of his right to put up contest in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case and, as such, could not take steps in the case and the case was decided against him ex parte. 

 45. Evidence, materials on record and fact and circumstances of the case manifest that fraud had been applied in objecting service of summons upon plaintiff-opposite party and by means of fraud he was kept in darkness of pre-emption proceeding against him. 

 47. Appellate Judge as last and final Judge of fact on consideration of evidences, especially evidence of DW 3, service return (Exhibit A), materials on record and fact and circumstances of the case and taking into stock legal aspect involved in case, adverting to decisions reached by learned Trial Judge and meditating Judicial Authority in Upendra Chandra Rishi and others vs Sufia Begum and others (Supra) recorded positive decision that summons of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case upon plaintiff-opposite party had not been served directly. Learned Appellate Judge further held that he believed that address of second-opposite party (plaintiff-opposite party) in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case had been concealed and that is nothing but fraud in the language of law and fraud having been practiced, Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1984 stood vitiated. On examination of decisions rendered, reasons counted in rendering decisions and conclusion reached by learned Appellate Judge it cannot be at all suggested that those went against weight of evidence and materials on record and suffer from patent illegality, legal infirmity and flagrant error of law. 

 A. Ex parte order dated 24-4-1988 recorded in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1984 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Kachua, Chandpur is set aside in respect of only plaintiff-opposite party Md Shafiullah Patwari but ex parte order recorded in respect of other three (3) Pre-emptees, Torab Ali Patwari, Shahidullah Patwari and Zitu Mia Patwari stands maintained. 

 B. Plaintiff-opposite party Md Shafiullah Patwari is not bound by ex parte order dated 24-4-1988 recorded in pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1984 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Kachua, Chandpur but other three (3) Pre-emptees namely, Turab Ali Patwari, Shahidullah Patwari and Zitu Mia Patwari are bound by ex parte order of pre-emption.
